properties.decision:
🛑 RECORDED AS `proposed` DELIBERATELY, AND IT MUST STAY THERE UNTIL ANTHONY SAYS OTHERWISE. This is the agent's judgement about how to model its own work, not his word — the same call made for `dec:an-interchangeable-backend-is-named-by-its-contract-not-by-a-function` on 2026-08-25, and for the same reason. A PROPOSED ruling PARKS NOTHING (there is a test pinning exactly that), so `cmp:upstream` goes on being reported as a part holding no function until this is accepted or replaced. That is correct behaviour, not a leak.

📌 The near-match offered was `cmp:upstream` itself — the PART this rules about. This is the ruling; that is the thing ruled on.

═══ THE SITUATION ═══

`cap:a-declared-dependency-is-watched-not-imported` is implemented across two modules. The JUDGEMENT — the declaration, the baseline, the comparison, what counts as `moved` — is in `crates/reflow2-core/src/depends.rs` (`cmp:depends`). The OBSERVATION — opening each declared upstream export and computing its content hash — is in `crates/reflow2-mcp/src/upstream.rs` (`cmp:upstream`). The split is FORCED: reflow2-core does no file I/O, deliberately and repeatedly.

The standing ruling (`chg:allocation-follows-the-code-not-the-neighbour`, 2026-08-25) says allocate to the module whose code implements the function, MOVE IT, DO NOT DUAL-ALLOCATE. Both halves are real code, so obeying it leaves one of the two modules empty whichever way it goes.

═══ THE PROPOSAL ═══

A module whose whole job is to SUPPLY AN OBSERVATION to a judgement living elsewhere is not an implementer of that judgement's function. It is the caller's half of a caller-supplies-the-observation split — the same shape in which `reconcile_dependencies` takes `observed` and `reconcile_artifacts` takes hashes. The function is "does the design I depend on differ from what I recorded"; reading a file is not that function, it is the material the function consumes.

So allocation stays on `cmp:depends`, and `cmp:upstream` is PARKED as deliberately empty.

═══ WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS WRONG, and it is not a small objection ═══

⚠️ **This is one loose reading away from a licence to leave anything empty.** "It only supplies input to something else" describes a great many modules, and applied loosely it becomes the excuse that quietly covers every unallocated part — the opposite of what the 2026-08-25 sweep achieved, which was to find 19 real functions hiding behind exactly that kind of reasoning. If accepted, the boundary must be stated tightly: NOT "helps another module", but "performs the I/O a deliberate no-I/O boundary forbids the judging module from doing, and makes no judgement of its own."

⚠️ **The alternative is not absurd.** `cmp:upstream` could carry a capability of its own — *"another design's record is read without opening its store"* — which is arguably a real function and is close to what `describe_designs` already does for `cmp:latent`. That means MORE parts and MORE capabilities, which cuts against the over-engineering instinct, but it is honest and needs no new ruling at all.

⚠️ **AND IT IS A LIVE INSTANCE OF AN OPEN QUESTION.** `dec:idea-a-capability-is-a-set-of-functions-and-a-black-box-delivers-functions` asks whether a capability should be a SET of functions across several parts, with a black box delivering functions rather than capabilities. This is exactly that case, arriving from real work rather than from thinking about the model — and if that question is answered YES, this ruling becomes unnecessary, because the capability would name both functions and both parts would hold one.

═══ OPTIONS ═══

(a) ACCEPT this ruling and park `cmp:upstream`, with the tight boundary above written into it.
(b) GIVE `cmp:upstream` ITS OWN CAPABILITY and allocate normally. No ruling needed; one more capability and one more part that is genuinely for something.
(c) DUAL-ALLOCATE to both parts, amending the 2026-08-25 ruling for the multi-module case specifically. Honest about the code, and it should amend that ruling rather than quietly break it.
(d) LEAVE IT UNALLOCATED AND UNRULED — reported as a defect until the black-box question is settled, on the grounds that a real open instance is more useful pressure on that question than a ruling that makes it comfortable.
properties.name: REJECTED — option (b) chosen instead: the reading half was given its own function, so no general rule about observation-suppliers was needed
properties.rationale:
SETTLED BY ANTHONY, 2026-08-28: option (b) — give `cmp:upstream` its own capability — with the explicit instruction to DEFINE THE NEED FIRST rather than mint the capability and back-fill a reason.

═══ WHY IT WAS RAISED (preserved from the original proposal, 2026-08-27) ═══
Raised because building `cap:a-declared-dependency-is-watched-not-imported` produced a genuinely empty part, and the standing allocation ruling gives no answer for a function that spans a deliberate architectural boundary. Left proposed because accepting it would be the agent ruling on the tidiness of its own work, which is precisely the case reserved for the user. The counter-arguments were written at full strength rather than as caveats, because this ruling's failure mode is that it GENERALISES: "supplies input to another module" would excuse nearly any empty part, and the 2026-08-25 sweep found 19 real functions behind that kind of reasoning. Option (d) was listed as a real option for the same reason — an open instance may be worth more than a comfortable answer.

═══ WHY (b) WON ═══
The proposal's own stated failure mode decided it: "supplies input to another module" describes a great many modules, and that reasoning has a 19-to-1 record of being the wrong read. A general rule with that record is a bad rule to accept off a single instance.

(a) WAS ALSO THE WRONG TOOL. Under UAF/DoDAF a resource performs FUNCTIONS and a capability emerges from functions across resources, so "reading a file is not a capability" is defensible doctrine — but reflow2 has no `Function` type, so (a) would have been a doctrine rule papering over a schema limitation. (b) works honestly inside the vocabulary that actually exists.

(c) was declined because it would break a working allocation ruling for one case. (d) was declined because parking a fully-explained defect as "pressure" degrades the defect list, and the pressure would have been aimed at adding a `Function` type to the schema — a change driven purely by reflow2's own design, which nobody using reflow2 has asked for. That is the wrench problem: do not reshape the tool because the tool's own model itched.

⭐ THE NEED WAS DEFINED FIRST, AND IT WAS NOT A NEW ONE. `cap:a-declared-upstream-is-read-where-it-lies` satisfies the already-accepted `req:design-dependencies-declared`, whose statement names the check "has what I depend on moved since" — unanswerable without opening the upstream file. No requirement was invented to justify the part. The separation of the reading half from the judging half is an ARCHITECTURAL CONSTRAINT (reflow2-core does no file I/O), not a separate need, and constraints do not need their own requirements.

📌 `dec:idea-a-capability-is-a-set-of-functions-and-a-black-box-delivers-functions` REMAINS OPEN and is untouched by this. It should be settled when a real user's design needs it, not because of one empty box in reflow2's own graph.
